articles.title: The Liberty’s Big 3 returned for unfinished business … and they’re getting to work
articles.summary: NEW YORK — White rally towels blanketed seats in Barclays Center pregame. It would soon be filled with nearly 18,000 raucous fans on Tuesday night, but for a...
articles.body:
NEW YORK — White rally towels blanketed seats in Barclays Center pregame.

It would soon be filled with nearly 18,000 raucous fans on Tuesday night, but for a moment there was a calm. When the storm hit, it was the Minnesota Lynx who were sent seeking shelter.

The initial surge came courtesy of Jonquel Jones , who scored the Liberty's first 7 points of the game, tirelessly working the offensive glass. Then came a cutting layup from Breanna Stewart off the assist from Sabrina Ionescu . It was Ionescu's turn next, scoring at the rim to give the Liberty a 10-point advantage less than five minutes into the game.

Every time the Lynx found respite, either Jones, Stewart or Ionescu was waiting. Sometimes it was all three. They combined for 60 points in the Liberty's historic 87-71 first-round Game 2 win over the Lynx , becoming the first No. 8 seed to eliminate a No. 1 seed in the WNBA playoffs. New York awaits the semifinals, where it will face the winner of the first-round matchup between the No. 4 Atlanta Dream and No. 5 Washington Mystics .

"When you have the three-headed monster coming at you, it's really tough," Stewart said. "Setting that tone every night is something that's important going forward because it's the playoffs."

When Jones, Stewart and Ionescu re-signed in free agency, they did so with the motivation of unfinished business.

After winning the franchise's first WNBA title in 2024 and then being eliminated in the first round last season, surely they were capable of more together.

The roller coaster of this 2026 season made what seemed like an obvious answer to that question uncertain. The Liberty entered the postseason with one more loss than last year, raising questions about how much more they could accomplish together.

On Tuesday night, they quieted the apprehension with their most complete game of the season. Despite their dominance, Ionescu said their best basketball is yet to come.

"It's when it matters most, now," Ionescu said. "When the stakes are high and you have to go on the road in a crazy environment and win a game and steal one, then you have to come here and not just get by, but get better because there's bigger goals that we have to accomplish."

For Ionescu, this season has been a particularly challenging slog. She started the campaign injured and has hinted that she has not been at 100 percent amid her poorest scoring output since the 2021 season. But entering Game 2 game, she said she had trust that the work she's put in would "come to light."

In front of a courtside celebrity crew that included rapper Meek Mill and WNBA legend Tina Charles , Ionescu radiated, finishing with 18 points on 4-of-10 shooting from 3-point range, and added seven assists and four rebounds. Her second 3-pointer of the night, a make from the left wing that put the Liberty up 47-35 just before the half, sent the rally towels spinning into the air and fans to their feet.

With a clear mind, Ionescu continued to heat up.

"That's kind of the best place to be as a shooter," Ionescu said. "When your minds empty and you're just playing. I just went out and obviously understood what the team needed and got the crowd into it."

Jones and Stewart added 21 points apiece. Jones cleaned up the boards, finishing with 13, and Stewart did a little bit of everything, adding five rebounds, four assists, two steals and two blocks to her stat line.

"What she does for us on the defensive end, late shot … we feel we need her on the floor," Liberty coach Chris DeMarco said. "It's that time. We manage it all season for this."

Stewart was the only constant for the Liberty during the regular season, putting them on her back in more ways than one. Beyond her production, she provided a steadiness amid instability as injuries threatened to derail their season. After the All-Star break, there was a moment when they had to confront reality and continue to believe in themselves.

"We are an eight seed," Stewart said. "Even though we don't feel like it. We need to be that. We have to have that chip on our shoulder and change the chip."

The Liberty were a nightmare matchup for the Lynx during the regular season, and that was once again the case in the first two games of the playoffs. Their length gave the Lynx problems, specifically rookie Olivia Miles, who played just 17 minutes, finishing with 5 points, two rebounds and one assist.

"Stewie, she freaking wins everything," Miles said. "She's very experienced. Sab has been here before, and J.J. obviously has been here, done this. Their size really bothered us. … It's a tough team. I'll be curious how they do the rest of the way just because of how much of a matchup nightmare they pose to other teams."

The Liberty are the first team to clinch a spot in the semifinals.

Both the Dream and Mystics have variations of a three-headed core that have steered their teams' successes. In Washington, that's been Shakira Austin , Kiki Iriafen and Sonia Citron . The Dream have Rhyne Howard , Allisha Gray and Angel Reese .

Both are higher seeds than the Liberty, but then again, the Liberty are not a typical eight seed.

"We're not listening to the outside noise," Jones said. "We understand that we can do a lot of great things. Coming into this series, yes there was seeding and that's because of the regular season. But we feel like we can play anybody and beat anybody. That's the mindset we have moving forward."

articles.title: D'Angelo Russell Lands Contract in Chinese Basketball Association After Grizzlies Release
articles.summary: D'Angelo Russell is headed to China after his release from the Memphis Grizzlies.
articles.body:
D'Angelo Russell is headed to China after his release from the Memphis Grizzlies.

Russell is joining the Shangai Sharks ahead of the Chinese Basketball Association's upcoming season, the league announced Wednesday.

The Washington Wizards traded Russell to the Grizzlies in July before the team waived him last week.

He had played 11 NBA seasons prior to being cut, most recently appearing in 26 games of the 2025-26 campaign for the Dallas Mavericks.

Initially selected by the Los Angeles Lakers with the No. 2 pick of the 2015 draft out of Ohio State, Russell later earned his first All-Star nod in 2019 with the Brooklyn Nets.

He has bounced around since that campaign in a series of trades that sent him to the Golden State Warriors and Minnesota Timberwolves. He returned to the Lakers and Nets before beginning last season with the Mavericks.

Russell most recently averaged 10.2 points and four assists per game while mostly coming off the bench for the Mavericks before falling out of Jason Kidd's rotation ahead of his inclusion in the Anthony Davis trade last February.

The 30-year-old did not play for the Wizards before he was dealt this summer to the Grizzlies, who made him a free agent by waiving him last week.

Russell will depart the NBA having averaged 17 points, 3.3 rebounds and 5.6 assists. He registered career shooting averages of 42.7 percent from the field and 36.3 percent from deep through 655 games.

The Sharks won the 2025-26 CBA championship in June to claim the team's first title since winning with Yao Ming 24 years ago.

The team's current roster features another former NBA player in Brandon Goodwin, who played four NBA seasons between 2018 and 2022. Former NBA center Hassan Whiteside won the championship with the club but is facing a potential ban from the league.

Other notable NBA players who played with the Sharks include Gilbert Arenas, Michael Beasley, Eric Bledsoe and Delonte West.

articles.title: Knicks' Karl-Anthony Towns Says He Looked at Milwaukee Homes on Zillow Amid Giannis Trade Rumors
articles.summary: Before the New York Knicks went on one of the great playoff runs in NBA history, there was a point in the 2025-26 season when it looked like they might have to break up their core by trading Karl-Anthony Towns because the formula didn't seem to be working.
articles.body:
Before the New York Knicks went on one of the great playoff runs in NBA history, there was a point in the 2025-26 season when it looked like they might have to break up their core by trading Karl-Anthony Towns because the formula didn't seem to be working.

Speaking to The Athletic's Jon Krawczynski , Towns admitted things got to the point that he started looking at homes in the Milwaukee area with his now-wife Jordyn Woods amid rumors the Knicks were interested in Giannis Antetokounmpo.

"We were on Zillow looking at Milwaukee," Towns said. "Like, 'Hey, babe, I went around town, and it's not that bad. This could be a good spot right here.'"

It's easy to forget now because of how the season ended, but the Knicks took a long time to figure things out under first-year head coach Mike Brown. The dynamic between Brown and Towns, in particular, seemed to be a source of some tension at times.

The Knicks' season hit its nadir on Jan. 19 when they lost by 17 to the Dallas Mavericks and were in the midst of a 2-9 stretch in 11 games.

Not long after that, reports circulated that the Knicks were among the teams trying to acquire Antetokounmpo if the Bucks decided to trade the superstar before the trade deadline.

Milwaukee ultimately held on to Antetokounmpo for the entire season. The Knicks' long addition at the deadline was acquiring Jose Alvarado from the New Orleans Pelicans.

Things did turn around for the Knicks after that rough patch. They won eight straight games after the Mavs' loss and closed the regular season 28-11 going into the playoffs.

The Knicks went 16-3 in the playoffs, including a run of 11 consecutive wins at one point, en route to winning their first championship in 53 years.

Towns averaged 15.9 points on 55.1 percent shooting (45.6 percent from three), 10.6 rebounds and 4.9 assists per game in the postseason.

Even though Towns ultimately didn't have to uproot his life last season, his long-term future with the Knicks remains unclear as the two sides are at odds in their talks for a new contract.

Towns is entering the final guaranteed year of his current deal, but there is a $61 million player option for 2027-28.

articles.title: New Jalen Duren Rumors Update Sign-and-Trade Talks amid Pistons Contract Buzz
articles.summary: After skipping media day and the start of training camp this week, Detroit Pistons center Jalen Duren's absence reportedly could extend into the 2026-27 season.
articles.body:
After skipping media day and the start of training camp this week, Detroit Pistons center Jalen Duren's absence reportedly could extend into the 2026-27 season.

Duren, who is a restricted free agent, has until Thursday to agree to a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer. He was eligible to receive a maximum offer of $287 million over five years, but the team reportedly offered him a five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed contract, which he has continued to reject.

The Athletic's Hunter Patterson reported that if the Pistons extend the deadline for the qualifying offer from Thursday, "there could be a scenario where Duren misses preseason and regular-season games if both sides are unable to decide on a new contract — though that'd seem extremely unprecedented and unlikely considering Duren's regular-season production."

Despite the ongoing stalemate , it doesn't sound like Detroit is motivated to get rid of the 22-year-old. Patterson noted, "As things stand, the Pistons have shown a reluctance to even engage in discussions around sign-and-trade packages for Duren."

Patterson and Sam Amick previously reported that the Sacramento Kings and Milwaukee Bucks "are known to be among the teams with serious interest" in trading for Duren, who was selected to his first All-Star Game last season.

For now, it appears that the Pistons are content to let things play out as Duren mulls his contract decision. Detroit will play its first preseason game against the Phoenix Suns on Oct. 5 before opening the regular season against the Boston Celtics on Oct. 20.

articles.title: Karl-Anthony Towns' Dad Rips Jimmy Butler, Says Knicks Star 'Bypassed' His Legacy After NBA Title
articles.summary: Even after watching his son, Karl-Anthony Towns, win the 2026 NBA championship with the New York Knicks, Karl Towns Sr. won't forget the past disrespect.
articles.body:
Even after watching his son, Karl-Anthony Towns, win the 2026 NBA championship with the New York Knicks, Karl Towns Sr. won't forget the past disrespect.

While speaking to The Athletic's Jon Krawczynski , the elder Towns called out Golden State Warriors veteran wing Jimmy Butler III and declared that his son surpassed his legacy by winning an NBA title.

"It only hurt me as a father to hear people saying stuff that was negative that wasn't true to bring him down," Karl Towns said. "But in the end, it all paid up. Jimmy ain't got no championship. Karl bypassed him."

Butler and Towns teamed together with the Minnesota Timberwolves during the 2017-18 season. Though their partnership was brief, it wasn't without some unforgettable controversy. After the Timberwolves opted to give contract extensions to Towns and Andrew Wiggins instead of Butler, the swingman demanded a trade and publicly criticized his teammates and coaches, famously calling Towns and Wiggins "soft" in an ESPN interview before he was traded to the Philadelphia 76ers in November 2018.

Krawczynski noted that at the time, some within the Timberwolves organization "quietly wanted to see Towns stand up for himself and fight back." However, the big man never engaged and refused to get into a public spat with Butler.

"I just was never going to change who I was, even when the world was asking me to change who I was, so I could be the character in their story," Towns told Krawczynski. "I just was going to continue to be me."

Still, the narrative painted by Butler would follow Towns for years. So when he finally broke through and helped lead the Knicks past the San Antonio Spurs in the 2026 NBA Finals, his father couldn't help but remember everything he had went through before reaching the pinnacle of the sport.

"When there were eight seconds to go in the game, I started crying because my emotions caught up to me," Karl Towns said. "As a dad, you sit here and you hear all the rumors. 'He can't do it. He's not tough. He'll never win a championship.'

"I knew in the next eight seconds, life was going to change. All the haters, all the naysayers, everybody who doubted him have to shut their mouths and respect him now."

articles.title: D'Angelo Russell leaves NBA, signs with China's Shanghai Sharks
articles.summary: Russell was released last week by the Grizzlies months after a July trade from the Wizards.
articles.body:
D'Angelo Russell has a new home and it will be in China.

Days after his release by the Memphis Grizzlies , the 30-year-old Russell has signed with the Shanghai Sharks of the China Basketball Association, the league announced on Wednesday .

Russell teased the move following his release last week by posting a video of his daughter saying "Ni Hao," which means "hello" in Chinese.

The Sharks are reigning CBA champions, taking home the franchise's first league title in 25 years last season. They are best known for being Yao Ming's team from 1997 to 2022 before the eight-time NBA All-Star was drafted by the Houston Rockets first overall in 2022.

Russell was the No. 2 overall pick by the Los Angeles Lakers in 2015. He would go on to play two stints with the franchise, as well as the Brooklyn Nets . He's also suited up for the Golden State Warriors , Minnesota Timberwolves and Dallas Mavericks .

He was voted on to the NBA All-Rookie Second Team in 2015-16, made the NBA All-Star Game in 2018-19 and was part of the 2023 Lakers NBA Cup-winning squad.

Russell played 26 games with the Mavericks last season, averaging a little over 19 minutes per night and 10.2 points, 4 assists and 2.3 rebounds. He was dealt to Memphis by the Washington Wizards in July as part of a trade involving six teams and 11 players .

After being dealt to the Wizards at the trade deadline, Russell did not play again during the 2025-26 season as the sides discussed a potential buyout. That never happened and he exercised his $6 million player option for this season before the summer trade.

articles.title: New NBA Rumors Update RJ Barrett's Raptors Contract Talks After Kawhi Leonard Trade
articles.summary: The Toronto Raptors reportedly opened training camp without having begun serious contract talks with RJ Barrett, according to Sportsnet's Michael Grange.
articles.body:
The Toronto Raptors reportedly opened training camp without having begun serious contract talks with RJ Barrett, according to Sportsnet's Michael Grange .

Grange reported Tuesday that "according to league sources, the Raptors and Barrett's long-time agent Bill Duffy have yet to sit down and have substantive conversations about the possibility of a contract extension."

He added there is still "optimism that Barrett's desire to get a deal that keeps him in Toronto long-term isn't one sided."

NBA Trade To Boost a New Eastern Conference Contender 🏀

Barrett is currently signed through next season under a $29.6 million cap hit before he is scheduled to hit unrestricted free agency next summer, per Spotrac . He expressed interest in staying in Toronto when speaking with reporters earlier this week.

The news comes just over a week after the delayed trade to acquire Kawhi Leonard from the Los Angeles Clippers was finalized .

The completion of the trade, which sent Brandon Ingram and Gradey Dick to Los Angeles, gave the Raptors a better understanding of what their salary cap looks like moving forward.

The franchise will be set to pay out $115 million to Leonard from 2027 to 2029 should he activate the player option on the back end of his new extension.

The Raptors have also committed significant money on long-term deals for Scottie Barnes, Immanuel Quickley and Jakob Poetl.

The franchise has about $178 million promised to that trio and Leonard alongside Collin Murray-Boyles, Allen Graves and Ja'Kobe Walter next season. Outside of those players, the Raptors are set next season to have about $35 million in space beneath the projected first luxury tax apron.

That could impact the Raptors' willingness to pay Barrett a maximum possible average annual salary of $44 million per season.

Raptors general manager Bobby Webster said last week he would consider exceeding the first apron this season if he felt his team was in position to win.

Barrett has played a starting role in Toronto since his acquisition from the New York Knicks in 2023, although he has missed significant time in each of his last two seasons.

The 26-year-old most recently averaged 19.3 points, 5.3 rebounds and 3.3 assists while shooting 49.1 percent from the field and 33.9 percent from deep through 57 games last season when not sidelined by injuries including knee and ankle issues.

He increased his production to 24.1 points, seven rebounds, four assists and 1.3 steals per playoff game before the Raptors were eliminated by the Cleveland Cavaliers in Game 7 of the 2026 first round.

Whether any progress is made on extensions negotiations, and if Leonard can help put the Raptors on track for another playoff run, could determine if the franchise ultimately considers placing Barrett and his expiring contract on the trade black ahead of the February 2027 deadline.

articles.title: Ultra Rare Kobe Bryant Signed Jersey with NBA Finals Patch Could Sell for Millions at Auction
articles.summary: A rare, No. 8 jersey worn by Kobe Bryant during the Los Angeles Lakers' 2004 NBA playoff run has officially hit the auction block.
articles.body:
A rare, No. 8 jersey worn by Kobe Bryant during the Los Angeles Lakers' 2004 NBA playoff run has officially hit the auction block.

The Realest announced Wednesday that it is auctioning off the jersey worn by Bryant while going a perfect 8-0 in the 2004 playoffs and 16-1 overall during the 2003-04 NBA season.

Based on photo matching, Bryant wore the jersey in each of the Lakers' series-clinching games against the Houston Rockets, San Antonio Spurs and Minnesota Timberwolves en route to the NBA Finals where they fell to the Detroit Pistons.

Per The Realest, the jersey is the only game-worn, No. 8 Bryant jersey that features the NBA Finals patch to ever come to market.

Autographed by the late Bryant, the jersey was originally auctioned off by the Lakers on Kobe's jersey retirement night on Dec. 8, 2017.

Based on the recent sold prices of game-worn, No. 8 Bryant jerseys, this particular jersey stands to sell for millions of dollars.

One sold for $7 million in 2025, another for $3.69 million in 2021, and a third for $2.73 million in 2022.

According to The Realest, the jersey currently up for bid is "the only documented No. 8 from after Bryant's rookie season to ever be offered publicly."

Bidding on Bryant's 2004 playoff jersey will end on Nov. 8 to commemorate Bryant's jersey number and the anniversary of the first double-digit scoring game of his NBA career.

articles.title: How to watch the 2026 WNBA Playoffs tonight: Game schedule, where to stream and more
articles.summary: Here's how to tune in to the 2026 WNBA playoffs.
articles.body:
The WNBA Playoffs began Sunday with eight of the top teams in the league competing for the 2026 championship title. The Minnesota Lynx , Golden State Valkyries , Atlanta Dream , Indiana Fever , New York Liberty , Washington Mystics , Dallas Wings and last year's champs, the Las Vegas Aces , have all made it into the playoffs. Both the Mystics and the Wings return to the playoffs after two seasons without qualification. To watch this year's playoff tournament, you'll need a variety of channels, including ABC, ESPN, NBC, and USA, along with Prime Video.

Tonight, you can catch the Dream vs. Mystics at 7 p.m. ET and the Valkyries vs. Wings at 9 p.m. — both games will air on ESPN. Here's what you need to know about the complete WNBA playoff schedule and how to watch every game.

What channels will the 2026 WNBA playoffs be on?

The WNBA playoffs will air across ABC, ESPN, ESPN2, USA, and NBC. The WNBA finals will be on NBC and USA.

articles.title: How Stephen Curry built his $350 million fortune? His $62.6M salary, $400M Li-Ning deal and lavish investments
articles.summary: Steph Curry has turned a remarkable NBA career into a vast business empire.
articles.body: Steph Curry has turned a remarkable NBA career into a vast business empire. The Golden State Warriors star is now estimated to have a net worth of $350 million, while his 2026-27 NBA salary stands at $62.6 million. His wealth extends far beyond basketball, with major endorsement deals, media ventures, investments and his own brand adding to his income. After more than a decade at the top of the sport, Curry has also secured another major contract that could take his career NBA earnings close to $650 million by 2029.Steph Curry net worth and NBA salaryCurry's current financial position reflects how much his value has grown since entering the NBA in 2009.The Warriors selected him seventh overall in the draft, and his first professional contract was modest compared with the deals he would later command. His breakthrough extension came in 2012, when Golden State gave him a four-year contract worth about $44 million.At the time, Curry was still dealing with concerns about recurring ankle problems. The contract soon became one of the most valuable bargains in NBA history. Curry developed into an MVP, won championships and changed the way teams approached three-point shooting while playing under that deal.His earning power changed dramatically in 2017. Curry signed a five-year, $201.2 million contract, becoming the first NBA player to agree to a deal worth more than $200 million.Four years later, he went even further. His four-year, $215 million extension made him the first player in league history to sign two contracts worth more than $200 million.Curry's latest extension arrived in September 2026. The two-year agreement is worth $116 million and begins with the 2027-28 season. It includes a player option for 2028-29.Based on those contracts, Curry's career NBA salary could reach approximately $648.7 million through the 2028-29 season if he exercises the option.Steph Curry's $400 million Li-Ning dealNBA salary is only one part of Curry's financial story. His endorsement portfolio has become just as important to his overall wealth.Curry started his professional career with Nike before moving to Under Armour in 2013. His rise to superstardom helped turn that relationship into a much larger business opportunity, eventually leading to Curry Brand.That partnership later changed. Curry Brand became independent after the relationship between Curry and Under Armour ended in 2025, although Under Armour continued selling previously developed products during 2026.Curry then landed another huge deal.In June 2026, he signed a 10-year endorsement agreement with Li-Ning worth more than $400 million. The partnership covers more than basketball shoes. It includes apparel, lifestyle products, golf and plans to expand Curry Brand retail operations in China and the United States.The agreement is worth more than $40 million per year on average, giving Curry another major source of income outside his Warriors contract.Celebrity Net Worth estimates that Curry also earns around $30 million annually from endorsements, although the exact amount can vary from year to year.His commercial portfolio includes partnerships with companies such as Fanatics, Google, JPMorgan Chase, Panini, Rakuten and 2K Sports.Steph Curry's business empire beyond basketballCurry has also built businesses that give him influence away from the court.His wider ventures operate under Thirty Ink, covering areas such as media, branding, investments and philanthropy. One of his best-known projects is Unanimous Media, which Curry founded with Erick Peyton in 2018.The company works across film, television, documentaries, publishing and podcasts. Its projects often focus on sports, family and faith.Curry has also explored entertainment in front of the camera. He played a fictionalised version of himself in the Peacock comedy "Mr. Throwback" and released the book "Shot Ready" in 2025.His business interests also include Gentleman's Cut bourbon and Underrated, a platform designed to give overlooked young athletes greater access to competition and development opportunities.That business approach has helped Curry build an identity that reaches well beyond his basketball statistics. His career has become a combination of sport, entertainment, branding and investment.Steph Curry's career, championships and real estateCurry's wealth would not be possible without the basketball career that created his global profile.He has won four NBA championships, two regular-season MVP awards and the 2022 NBA Finals MVP. He was also the first unanimous MVP in NBA history after his historic 2015-16 campaign.That season remains one of the most memorable individual years in modern NBA history. Curry averaged 30.1 points per game, made 402 three-pointers and helped Golden State win 73 regular-season games.In 2021, he passed Ray Allen to become the NBA's career leader in made three-pointers. He later reached another historic milestone by becoming the first player to make 4,000 regular-season three-pointers in March 2025.Curry added an Olympic gold medal to his résumé at the 2024 Paris Games, helping Team USA win the men's basketball tournament.His success has also shaped his property portfolio. Curry and his wife, Ayesha, have completed several major real estate transactions in California.Among their notable purchases was a $31 million Atherton estate bought in 2019. They later sold another Atherton property for $29.1 million in May 2026 after purchasing it for $30 million in 2020.The couple have also owned homes in Oakland, Orinda, Walnut Creek, Alamo and Menlo Park, along with a luxury condominium in San Francisco.Away from business and basketball, Curry and Ayesha have focused heavily on philanthropy. They founded the Eat. Learn. Play. Foundation, which supports children through programmes involving food, education and physical activity.Curry's financial rise therefore tells a larger story than a list of contracts. articles.title: Mariona Ortiz deja el Casademont Zaragoza por el Project B
articles.standfirst: La oferta irrechazable en lo económico para la capitana deja al equipo aragonés sin su referente días antes de empezar la Liga Femenina Endesa
articles.summary: La oferta irrechazable en lo económico para la capitana deja al equipo aragonés sin su referente días antes de empezar la Liga Femenina Endesa
articles.body: Mariona Ortiz, base internacional del Casademont Zaragoza, ha comunicado al club aragonés su intención de dejar la entidad con el objetivo de fichar por Project B, la revolucionaria Liga mundial de baloncesto femenino de élite que arrancará en enero de 2027. La jugadora de 34 años, reciente medalla de bronce con la selección en el Mundial de Berlín 2026, ha recibido una oferta "irrechazable" y pagará su cláusula para enrolarse en la competición donde coincidirá, entre otras, con Awa Fam. Las jugadoras de la selección son élite. Ortiz discute en estos días cuando dejará el club aragonés, en un momento difícil para el equipo que dirige Carlos Cantero, con el mercado cerrado y la Liga Femenina Endesa a punto de arrancar (lo hace este fin de semana). El Casademont Zaragoza, que celebra esta temporada su 25 aniversario, juega también la Euroliga y es el anfitrión de la Final a 6 de 2027 en el Príncipe Felipe. Las dos opciones para la catalana pasan por dejar ya el equipo y esperar a enero para iniciar su nueva etapa profesional o seguir jugando con el equipo aragonés hasta que lo permita su nuevo contrato con Project B. Las dentelladas de Project B son tremendas. En lo económico, como la NCAA, es imbatible. Un contrato medio bordea los 500.000 euros, unas cifras inalcanzables en el contexto de la Liga Femenina Endesa. La competición estará compuesta por seis equipos de once jugadoras con una serie de torneos itinerantes, como si fueran Grandes Premios de F1. Tokio y Valencia ya están confirmadas como sedes y la lista de estrellas es lujosa: Alysa Thomas, Ogwumike, que fue MVP de la WNBA, Jewell Lloyd, Jonquel Jones, Fiebich, Ayayi... El proyecto tiene grandes inversores detrás como Russell Westbrook, Candance Parker y Novak Djokovic. A falta de un año para terminar su contrato y en una época de su vida deportiva donde ya no necesita demostrar apenas nada, después de haber contribuido a llevar al Zaragoza (con el que ganó la Copa de la Reina en 2023) a la élite europea, Mariona está en condiciones de recoger en lo económico todo lo que ha sembrado estos años con su buen baloncesto, su profesionalidad y su liderazgo. El Casademont, mientras, pierde su faro.

articles.title: La Euroliga blinda a sus árbitros hasta 2029
articles.standfirst: La competición cierra filas y se alinea con sus principales actores deportivos -jugadores, entrenadores y árbitros- para afrontar una nueva era de crecimiento
articles.summary: La competición cierra filas y se alinea con sus principales actores deportivos -jugadores, entrenadores y árbitros- para afrontar una nueva era de crecimiento
articles.body: la Euroliga y la Unión de Árbitros de la Euroliga (UEBO) han renovado oficialmente su convenio colectivo, reforzando una relación que consideran clave para el desarrollo y la profesionalización del arbitraje en el baloncesto europeo. El acuerdo permanecerá vigente hasta el final de la temporada 2028-29. El pacto fue firmado en la sede de la Euroliga por su CEO, Chus Bueno, y el presidente de la UEBO, Sreten Radovic, con la presencia de representantes de ambas organizaciones. El nuevo acuerdo busca mantener actualizado el marco que regula su relación ante la evolución de las competiciones, el creciente papel de los árbitros y los avances tecnológicos aplicados al arbitraje. Uno de los pilares del convenio es establecer un marco estable y homogéneo para los árbitros, fijando principios, condiciones de trabajo y compromisos mutuos que afectan a su labor tanto en la Euroliga como en la Eurocup. La renovación pretende aportar seguridad y estabilidad a los colegiados mientras ambas partes continúan trabajando en la evolución del arbitraje. La tecnología ocupa también un lugar destacado. El acuerdo mantiene el compromiso con la mejora continua de los procesos arbitrales y con la incorporación de nuevas herramientas destinadas a ayudar a los colegiados en su trabajo. Chus Bueno subraya que los árbitros necesitan un marco profesional, recursos y tecnología para poder desempeñar su labor al máximo nivel. El nuevo convenio da continuidad a una estructura que comenzó en 2019 y fue renovada en 2023. Junto a los acuerdos existentes con la asociación de jugadores (ELPA) y el recientemente firmado con el comité de entrenadores (EHCB), el pacto con la UEBO completa un entramado destinado a alinear a la Euroliga con sus principales actores deportivos —jugadores, entrenadores y árbitros— mientras la competición afronta una nueva etapa de crecimiento.

articles.title: Prime Video WNBA broadcast crew embarrasses itself with coverage of A'ja Wilson fan incident
articles.summary: Prime Video's panel blamed an Indiana Fever fan after A'ja Wilson's confrontation, but arena security found no Fan Code of Conduct violation.
articles.body: Prime Video's coverage of Tuesday's Aces-Fever playoff game came with a remarkably simple explanation for A'ja Wilson's confrontation with a fan: Wilson was upset, so the fan must have done something wrong. The Fever, however, said arena security spoke with the fan and witnesses and found no violation of the Fan Code of Conduct. The team's statement never made it into Prime's postgame discussion. ACES' A'JA WILSON GETS TECH FOR CONFRONTATION WITH FEVER FAN, WHO WAS DETERMINED TO HAVE BROKEN NO RULES "Following a report of a comment directed toward a player, arena security spoke with the fan involved and witnesses. Security determined there was no violation of the Fan Code of Conduct, the fan was not removed from the arena. We consider the matter closed," the team said. A nearby spectator told OutKick the fan was disputing the foul call while pointing at Wilson. Wilson received a technical foul after the fourth-quarter confrontation during Indiana's 99-89 victory, which tied the series at one game apiece. Prime's broadcasters immediately defended her reaction without establishing what the fan had done to warrant it. "We don't know what was said" Following the incident, color analyst Candace Parker acknowledged, "We don't know what was said." But that didn't stop fellow analyst LaChina Robinson from describing Wilson's reaction as "not even in line with her demeanor unless it's absolutely necessary." Absolutely necessary? How could Robinson know that from watching Wilson react? And it's not as if there was no context available, either. Watching live, I noticed an arena security guard seated directly in front of the fan. He didn't react or stand up until Wilson had aggressively crossed the baseline, and the fan was already seated by then. One might think a security guard sitting directly in front of a fan would intervene if he heard something inappropriate or saw the fan enter an area where he wasn't allowed. That would have been useful context for the broadcast to note. Instead, the broadcast treated Wilson's reaction as the only one that mattered. Play-by-play announcer Michael Grady described the stoppage as officials clearing things up and getting "this fan out of the building." The fan was not removed from the arena, according to the Fever. Parker also invoked previous incidents, saying, "I feel like this has happened several times here in Indiana." Well, previous complaints about Indiana fans haven't always held up under investigation. In August, after Aces guard Jackie Young complained about a fan during a game in Indiana, the Fever said security found no Fan Code of Conduct violation. The team said that fan was not removed from the arena but elected to leave. ACES STAR TARGETS HECKLING FEVER FANS IN INDY BEFORE CHELSEA GRAY STUNS CAITLIN CLARK IN OT THRILLER Last year, the WNBA investigated allegations of racist behavior by Fever fans toward Angel Reese and said those allegations were not substantiated. In that case, it was ESPN rushing to embrace those allegations before the investigation was complete. Parker didn't identify which incidents she meant. But prior complaints don't become proof of fan misconduct just because a broadcaster brings them up again. Prime's postgame panel doubled down on blaming the fan By the postgame show, Prime had more time to gather information. Lindsey Harding instead offered viewers certainty based on her familiarity with Wilson. "I know something was said. Something was said, disrespectful, to a point for her to do that, and it's not okay," Harding said. OK, what was it? Harding didn't identify the comment. She went on to say, "It's always a player that gets attacked and has to stand up for themselves. And you know what? She stood up for herself, and she got a technical foul for that." Harding described Wilson as defending herself without establishing that the fan attacked her. Swin Cash also relied on Wilson's character, telling viewers, "So whatever was said, whether it was pointing, something happened." Teresa Weatherspoon referred to "the words that were possibly said" before telling the fan to "back that crap up and sit down." Host Allie Clifton responded, "Well said by all three of you," without pushing back on any of them, even though all three made claims that deserved further inspection. Clifton then clarified that the fan remained in the arena and was not ejected. But the discussion never addressed security's finding that he had not violated the Fan Code of Conduct. The Fever's statement was circulating on X by 8:53 p.m. ET, roughly 15 minutes before Prime's postgame discussion began. Wilson's explanation didn't support Harding's claim Prime then aired part of Wilson's explanation, which focused on the fan's movements and pointing. "I don't give a damn what you said. I don't give a damn how you said it, the tone. That is unacceptable," Wilson said. Wilson was describing her objection to a "man" stepping toward her. Her account did not support Harding's claim that the fan had made a disrespectful comment. Nor does a player's objection to being pointed at establish that a fan broke arena rules. Cash responded to the clip by saying, "Now, there may have been other things that were said and whatnot." Oh, OK. Wilson focused on the fan stepping toward her and pointing, but Cash still wanted to speculate about "other things" he might have said. What information supported that speculation? They also didn't take Wilson to task for escalating the exchange, overreacting to standard sports fan behavior, and costing her team a technical foul at a crucial late-game moment. CAITLIN CLARK'S TECHNICAL FOUL SPARKS FURIOUS RALLY AS FEVER AVOID ELIMINATION AGAINST ACES Of the seven Prime broadcasters, not one raised the most likely explanation: Wilson was frustrated with the way the game was going and took it out on a fan. She had dominated Game 1 with 38 points and 16 rebounds. At the time of the confrontation in Game 2, she had 14 points and the Aces trailed by 11 with 4:10 remaining. Indiana fans have become an easy scapegoat, and the reaction on Bluesky showed how little information some people needed to blame them. One user wrote, "I don't really care what the fan said. If it upset Wilson that much, toss him." Another demanded that Wilson's technical be rescinded and blamed "racist bastards." I wouldn't be surprised if Wilson expected people around the WNBA to rush to her defense in a confrontation with a Fever fan. Prime's panel certainly obliged. And for all the talk about diversity in sports television, where was the diversity of thought? Prime's seven broadcasters included five Black women, one Black man and one White woman, yet nobody in the game or postgame discussion challenged the assumption that the fan must have done something wrong. Seven different people reached roughly the same conclusion because that's what happens when "diversity" means "not White men" instead of diversity of thought. OutKick asked the Fever whether the guard seated in front of the fan was among the witnesses security interviewed and what its review established about the fan's words and movements. We also asked when the team provided its findings to Prime. The Fever did not respond to those follow-up questions before publication. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! OutKick asked Prime to explain the reporting behind its commentators' assertions and account for its handling of the Fever's statement. Prime did not respond before publication. Seeking the Fever's account was a basic reporting obligation. The panel spent several minutes condemning a fan without presenting arena security’s finding that the fan had not violated the conduct code. That's a complete dereliction of journalistic duty. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER Harding told viewers, "I know." OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD It's pretty easy to "know" when you've decided the outcome without needing to see any proof.

articles.title: Suns' Dillon Brooks Charged with DUI Stemming from Incident in March
articles.summary: PHOENIX (AP) — Phoenix Suns forward Dillon Brooks has been charged with driving under the influence related to his arrest in March by police in Scottsdale, Arizona.
articles.body:
PHOENIX (AP) — Phoenix Suns forward Dillon Brooks has been charged with driving under the influence related to his arrest in March by police in Scottsdale, Arizona.

Online court records show that Brooks has a court date on Oct. 28 for the the Class 1 misdemeanor charge.

"This charge stems from the incident last March," Suns senior vice president of communications Stacey Mitch said in a statement. "We have addressed the matter with Dillon and have no further comment."

Brooks was arrested during a traffic stop on March 6 at roughly 1 a.m. and after an investigation, he was taken to jail. He was released following the booking process around 3:30 a.m.

The 30-year-old was out with a fractured left hand at the time. He averaged a career-high 20.2 points per game last season and signed a $73 million, three-year extension during the offseason that will keep him with the team through 2030.

Brooks is also facing separate misdemeanor reckless driving and speeding charges related to an arrest in January. The court date for that case is Nov. 9.

ESPN first reported the developments in the cases.

articles.title: Everything Giannis Said About Heat Training Camp, Injury Status, Facing Bucks After Trade and More
articles.summary: Giannis Antetokounmpo says his first training camp with the Miami Heat has so far been "everything that I expected and more."
articles.body:
Giannis Antetokounmpo says his first training camp with the Miami Heat has so far been "everything that I expected and more."

"Chemistry-wise, it's great, and it's only going to get better," Antetokounmpo told reporters Wednesday (h/t ClutchPoints' Zachary Weinberger ).

Antetokounmpo added he has already benefitted in training camp scrimmages from playing against players like Bam Adebayo, Bobby Portis and Nick Richards in practice.

"When you play against a guy like Bobby, or Nick, or Bam, you're only going to get better," Antetokounmpo said.

Antetokounmpo continued, per Weinberger: "I'm having fun. Guys are competing. Guys are playing the right way. Guys are playing together."

The Heat star used almost the opposite descriptions when speaking about the Bucks following a January loss last season that would turn out to be one of his final games with the franchise.

"We're not playing hard," Antetokounmpo said about the Bucks at the time. "We aren't doing the right thing. We're not playing to win. We're not playing together. Our chemistry's not there."

Antetokounmpo ultimately sat out most of the remainder of last season before he was traded to the Heat in July.

He seems to be hoping for a different experience in Miami, where he said Wednesday the team plays in a way "totally different to what I've been used to."

"I feel like this group's very competitive. I see the way these guys move," Antetokounmpo said about the Heat's defense. "They move so f--king fast, it's insane... I don't know if they've trained under this culture for many years, and they're just used to this speed."

Antetokounmpo also said Wednesday he feels "good" after playing just 36 games last season amid injury issues prior to his trade.

He missed significant time last season due to calf injuries, although he disputed down the stretch whether the Bucks were holding him out at their own discretion.

"I've been unlucky, a lot of times... I keep on moving forward, keep on finding ways to improve my skills and also improve my body," Antetokounmpo said about his injury history. "I worked hard, changed my diet. Hopefully it works."

Antetokounmpo is preparing to open his first season with the Heat Oct. 21 before playing the visiting Bucks for the first time as an opponent Nov. 18.

Jan. 28 marks the first time Antetokounmpo is scheduled to travel to play his first game as a visitor at Milwaukee.

"I think going back in a different uniform, and going through the hallway, and seeing the familiar faces, for sure, it's going to be difficult," Antetokounmpo said about his return to his former city. "But at the end of the day.. I'm a guy that lives with no regret, and when I get there, I'm going to try to put on a show."

Antetokounmpo spent 13 seasons with the Bucks before he was traded to the Heat, where he will be eligible to sign an extension in January.

The likelihood Antetokounmpo makes a long-term commitment to his new franchise could be influenced by whether the new Heat starting lineup of Davion Mitchell, Klay Thompson and Andrew Wiggins alongside Antetokounmpo and Adebayo is able to solidify this team's status as title contender over the first half of the upcoming season.

articles.title: Extending WNBA Playoffs Would Cost Owners Up to $1 Million in Player Pay
articles.summary: The No. 1–seeded Lynx exited the playoffs after just two games.
articles.body:
On Tuesday night, the New York Liberty sealed a two-game first-round sweep over the Minnesota Lynx with an 87–71 victory at the Barclays Center, marking the first time a No. 8 seed has upset a No. 1 seed since the WNBA switched to an eight-team, conference-less format in 2022.

The Lynx, which finished the regular season with a 33–11 record, exited the playoffs after playing just one home and one road game, prompting renewed questions over the WNBA's postseason format.

The league switched to a 1-1-1 format for the first round last season, after the previous 2–1 format drew some criticism for failing to guarantee each playoff team at least one home game. However, some coaches and players have recently pushed back against the new format, arguing that either a different hosting setup or a longer series would provide a more significant competitive advantage to the higher seed. (MLB also has a three-game first round, with all three games played at the higher seed.)

"The 1-1-1, I don't think is a good setup," Aces coach Becky Hammon said earlier this month after a late-regular-season victory over the Storm. "It should be 2-1 or go to a five-game series, because the 1-1-1 is no advantage for the higher seed, really. It's nothing. That's not my decision obviously, but I don't like the setup in that first round."

Four-time All-Star Liberty guard Sabrina Ionescu expressed a similar sentiment in a press conference last week, foreshadowing her team's upset victory.

"It needs to be 2–1 or go to a five-game series, as I think anything can happen in a 1-1-1," Ionescu said. "The team gets hot, the team plays well, and then yeah."

Fever coach Stephanie White added to the chorus last week, calling the 1-1-1 format "probably the best of the worst-case scenario."

"I prefer a longer series," White said. "It wouldn't be as challenging if the WNBA had Eastern and Western conferences, but it doesn't, so teams are crossing the country half the time. It's certainly an imperfect system."

There is recent precedent for the WNBA expanding playoff series length. The league implemented a best-of-seven WNBA Finals for the first time in its history last year after 20 years of best-of-five finals.

Yet, any further attempts to add playoff games may be complicated by the league's collective bargaining agreement. The CBA says that an increase in the number of possible playoff games must be accompanied by a proportional increase in merit-based player bonuses, and the league must consult with the players' union before finalizing any changes.

Article XXXIII Section 5 of the CBA states: "If the maximum number of possible playoff games increases beyond twenty-nine (29), the merit bonuses related to playoff achievement of a Team set forth in Article IX hereof shall be increased proportionally." (The league already is at a maximum of 29 total playoff games.)

As is the case in most pro sports leagues, WNBA players are paid their salaries for the regular season, not the playoffs. Each player on a playoff team gets a bonus depending on how far their team makes it:

The champion and runner-up bonuses are double that of the Commissioner's Cup, the in-season tournament that awards $30,000 to the players of the winning team and $10,000 for each player on the runner-up side.

If the WNBA expanded the first round to a five-game series, that would mean the maximum number of playoff games league-wide would be 37—a 27% increase in games. The CBA indicates that an increase in playoff games, even in just one round, would affect "each of the per-player merit bonuses." So a 27% increase in player bonuses would mean:

Other possible scenarios would be to increase the second-round series to seven games or even to bring all series to seven games. The bonuses would look like this for each scenario:

Assuming 12 players per team, this year's total playoff bonus payout will be $1.44 million. A change to a best-of-five first-round series would increase the pot by about $400,000.

A change to best-of-seven format across all three rounds would bring the total prize pool to an estimated $2.43 million, about $1 million more than the current amount.

But the league also needs to take into account how the increased number of games will affect the schedule. The 2026 WNBA Finals will end on Oct. 31 at the latest. But next year, the regular season will jump from 44 to 50 games, which could push the end of the season into November. In 2029, the season is expected to increase to a 52-game schedule.

The CBA states that starting next year, the WNBA season, including playoffs, can run until Nov. 21. This can be pushed to Nov. 30 in 2028, because the Olympics are that summer.

As for the start of the season, the CBA states the earliest that training camp can begin is April 1, and the season must start within 30 days of training camp. That gives the league a maximum of six months to fit the 50- or 52-game regular season and any expanded playoff format.

It would be challenging, though, for the league to start much earlier than its usual early-May tip-off. In 2026, for example, UCLA won the Division I women's title on April 5, the draft was held on April 13, camps opened on April 19, and the regular season started just 19 days later, on May 8.

articles.title: Problema de cupos para el Unicaja con la lesión de Alberto Díaz
articles.standfirst: Vidorreta dispone solo de cuatro jugadores de formación y en la BCL necesitan cinco
articles.summary: Vidorreta dispone solo de cuatro jugadores de formación y en la BCL necesitan cinco
articles.body: El Unicaja salió reforzado en sensaciones de su estreno en la Liga Endesa ante el Real Madrid, pese a la derrota por apenas dos puntos. Los de Txus Vidorreta tuvieron opciones hasta los últimos instantes para llevarse el triunfo y dejaron argumentos para el optimismo. La nota negativa, sin embargo, fue importante: la lesión de Alberto Díaz. El base malagueño terminó el encuentro con molestias en el isquio de su pierna izquierda y las pruebas médicas han confirmado una lesión que le mantendrá alejado de las pistas entre seis y ocho semanas. Un contratiempo que, además de afectar a la rotación, genera un problema añadido pensando en la BCL, donde el Unicaja debutará el próximo 7 de octubre en Lituania. La caída de Alberto deja a Vidorreta con cuatro jugadores de formación disponibles: Pantzar, Djedovic, Barreiro y Willy Hernangómez. Son suficientes para cumplir con el cupo exigido en la Liga Endesa, que obliga a contar con cuatro jugadores de esta condición, pero no para la Basketball Champions League, donde deben ser cinco los jugadores de formación incluidos en la convocatoria. La situación obliga al Unicaja a mirar al mercado con una doble necesidad. El club ya tiene algunas posiciones más debilitadas por las bajas de Nzosa y Tyson Pérez, pero ahora aparece también la obligación de incorporar, llegado el caso, a un jugador que cumpla con la condición de cupo. Uno de los nombres que aparece sobre la mesa es el de Yankuba Sima. El pívot del Valencia Basket no entra en los planes de Xavi Albert y volvió a quedarse fuera de la convocatoria este domingo ante el Lleida. Tampoco viajó con el conjunto taronja a Turquía para el estreno europeo ante el Besiktas. Su incorporación permitiría, además, reforzar una posición interior que también necesita efectivos. Otra posibilidad pasa por mirar hacia abajo. El pasado curso, Ibon Navarro ya recurrió en determinados encuentros a jugadores como Manu Trujillo o Butajevas, que se entrenaban con el primer equipo pese a competir habitualmente con el conjunto de Liga U. Ahora, con Alberto Díaz fuera, uno de los nombres que podría ganar protagonismo es el de Alonso de la Iglesia. El joven talento acaba de cumplir 16 años y es considerado uno de los proyectos con mayor futuro de la cantera cajista. Eso sí, su situación física también genera dudas después de sufrir una molestia en el hombro frente al Obradoiro en la primera jornada de la competición sub-22, partido que no pudo terminar.
